deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside Grothendieck's c.1984 notes on when a tensor category is rigid, a Tannakian-type question. Its two neighbouring sheets are unrelated documents (a publisher's contract and a DEA notice of 10 Oct 1984).

1. Example (top of page). Take C = Mod_f(k), finite k-modules. Take F = the fibre functor M ↦ M ⊗_k k' with values in Mod(k'), for an extension k'/k (finite, as later used).
- The object U representing the endomorphisms/coendomorphisms of F is U = k' ⊗_k k'.
- U carries a co-algebra(-oid) structure over k'. Its canonical counit is ε : k'⊗k' → k', the multiplication map.
- The k'-dual is A = U^{∨(k')} ≃ Hom_k(k',k') ≃ End_k(k'). Its 'usual' ring structure is composition of k-endomorphisms.
- In modern terms, U is Sweedler's canonical (descent) coring of k'/k. A is its dual ring, the descent ring End_k(k').

2. Marginal NB, under the hypothesis k'/k finite.
- One recovers U ≃ A^{∨(k)}.
- The comultiplication Δ_U : U → U ⊗ U is the transpose of the multiplication A⊗A → A, which comes from F.
- Associativity of A corresponds to coassociativity of Δ_U.
- This is the standard algebra/coalgebra (ring/coring) duality in the finite case.

3. The programme (below the rule). Grothendieck seeks intrinsic conditions on the tensor category C, with its ⊗ exact, ensuring the following. For U attached to k'/k and F as above, the functor on finite-type modules over A (written over the line also as U⊗k'), M' ↦ M' ⊗_{k'⊗_k k'} k', should be exact and faithful.
- He remarks that exactness is OK if k'/k is étale.
- He then asks whether one needs C rigid and k ≅ End_C(1_C) ('???').
- He sets the task 'Exprimer la rigidité de C !'

4. What this serves. In modern terms it is the descent step in a Tannaka/Saavedra/Deligne reconstruction with a fibre functor over an extension k' ≠ k. One wants to identify C with comodules over the groupoid or coalgebroid U, i.e. with descent data. The question is which internal properties of C (rigidity, End(1)=k) make this descent functor exact and faithful.
errors: Exactness when k'/k is finite étale is fine: k'⊗_k k' is then a product of fields, k' is a projective factor, and M' ↦ M'⊗_{k'⊗k'} k' is exact.

Faithfulness fails on all k'⊗_k k'-modules: the functor kills modules supported on the other factors. So faithfulness can only hold on a restricted class of modules (those coming from descent data or from C); the page leaves this implicit.

For inseparable k'/k, k'⊗_k k' is local Artinian and k' is not flat over it, so exactness genuinely fails. The '(OK si étale)' restriction is consistent with this, but nothing is said about the general case.
The identifications A ≃ End_k(k') and U ≃ A^{∨(k)} need k'/k finite. This is only stated in the margin.
There is some ambiguity in the transcription: the 'A-modules' versus the k'⊗_k k'-modules actually used in the formula M'⊗_{k'⊗k'}k'.

ideas.what: The coendomorphism object of the fibre functor M ↦ M⊗_k k' on Mod_f(k) is k'⊗_k k', with counit given by multiplication.
ideas.modern_name: Sweedler's canonical (descent) coring / the groupoid Spec(k'⊗_k k') ⇉ Spec k' of a fibre functor over k'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sweedler (1975, canonical coring); Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne ('Catégories tannakiennes', 1990) for fibre functors over k'
ideas.where_published: Descent along k'/k is in SGA1 VIII / FGA (descente fidèlement plate); the coalgebroid formulation does not appear in his published texts as far as known

ideas.what: The dual ring A = End_k(k') and the duality between multiplication on A and comultiplication on U (associativity ↔ coassociativity).
ideas.modern_name: Ring/coring duality; descent ring End_k(k') (Morita form of Galois descent)

ideas.what: Seek intrinsic conditions on a tensor category (rigidity, End(1)=k) making the descent functor M' ↦ M'⊗_{k'⊗k'}k' exact and faithful; 'express rigidity of C'.
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian recognition with fibre functor over an extension; rigidity of abelian tensor categories (Deligne's criteria)
ideas.where_published: Tannakian ideas are in Grothendieck's program as carried out by Saavedra; not in his own published texts in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates in 1984 the problem of characterising intrinsically, in terms of the tensor category alone, when descent along a fibre functor over k' is exact and faithful. He asks whether rigidity and End(1)=k are necessary. This is essentially the question Deligne answered in 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990), so it documents Grothendieck working on the same problem independently around that time. It does not appear to contain a result absent from the literature.
missed.quote: Il faut il que C soit rigide, et que k ⥲ End_C(1_C) ??? ... Exprimer la rigidité de C !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck's own c.1984 engagement with rigidity and Tannakian recognition, contemporaneous with Deligne's work. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The example (k'⊗_k k' as descent coring, End_k(k') as its dual ring) is standard. The question posed was answered by Deligne (1990). The interest is mainly historical: Grothendieck was revisiting Tannakian rigidity around 1984.

'structure de k-cog. suivie canonique ε' is probably 'structure de k'-cog[èbre] (co-unité canonique ε : k'⊗k' → k')'.
'pour la structure d'anneau la [?] habituelle' probably means 'la [loi de composition / structure] habituelle' of End_k(k').
Margin NB: probably 'dans l'hyp. k'/k fini et C..., U ≃ A^{∨(k)}', 'transposé de la multiplication A⊗_k A → A', and 'associativité ⟺ co-associativité de Δ_U'.
'On cherche conditions intrinsèques sur C (le ⊗ exact) qui assurent que pour U comme ... k'/k et F comme dessus, le foncteur des A-modules (A = U⊗_k k') de t.f.' — 'fonction' should be 'foncteur'.
'(OK si k'/k est étale) et fidèle.'
